newsitem.title: USA: APL shares jump on Neptune Orient buyout.
newsitem.headline: APL shares jump on Neptune Orient buyout.

text.p: The stock of APL Ltd. surged about 40 percent Monday on news that the container carrier has agreed to be acquired by Singaporean shipping firm Neptune Orient Lines Ltd. in a deal worth $825 million.
The stock jumped $8.375 to $29.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The acquisition, announced over the weekend, values APL at $33.50 per share.
The merged company would have revenues of more than $4 billion, making it one of the largest shipping companies in the world.
APL will retain its name and continue its transportation operations, headed by its existing management in Oakland, Calif.
Neptune Orient said Monday the takeover would hurt its earnings for 1997, but it declined to say what costs it would incur from the merger.
The firms will operate a total fleet of 113 vessels, including 76 container ships.
Neptune Orient employs about 4,800 people worldwide, while based APL has about 4,000 employees.
